purpose: Model how legacy sovereign/household/corporate debt denominated in an incumbent currency behaves during a monetary regime transition.

channels.mechanism: Unexpected inflation in the legacy currency reduces the real burden of fixed nominal claims while transferring wealth from nominal creditors to nominal debtors.
Once inflation/devaluation is expected, new nominal borrowing rates and risk premia may rise, limiting repeated use of surprise dilution.
Legacy debt may be voluntarily exchanged for K-denominated claims under explicit terms.
A treasury/fund may purchase legacy claims at market prices and retire or restructure them.
Possible only under applicable legal authority and contract terms; never assumed by this model.

guardrails: Do not model deliberate deception or market manipulation as a policy instrument.
Every debt reduction must identify the corresponding creditor-side asset loss, transfer, restructuring or buyback cost.
Foreign-currency and inflation-indexed debt are modeled separately from fixed nominal domestic-currency debt.
accounting_identity: A liability extinguished, written down or inflated away corresponds to a change in another sector’s financial asset position.
